title: New Foremen Onboarding
body: Push a newly promoted foreman straight into running a shift without the structured buildup, and the gaps show up exactly where ADW's NCR corpus already flags them — Stage 4, Stage 6, ROM pad — supervisors present but not catching or stopping the problem in time.
keyPoints: Four pillars get rated at final assessment: technical competence, safety and compliance leadership, leadership and communication, and shift control/decision-making.

The four weeks build in order — orientation and shadowing (Week 1), field skills and NCR writing (Week 2), coaching and emergency response (Week 3), independent shift control (Week 4). Skipping ahead defeats the point.
The Week 4 readiness call is three-way, not pass/fail: ready for full duties, ready with support and oversight, or not yet ready with another training block before reassessment.
The job isn't done at Week 4 — the 90-day plan (weekly check-ins, monthly KPI review, peer mentoring) is what actually locks the habits in.
Shift handover gets taught in Week 1 on purpose — incidents cluster at shift start and end, and that's a handover-discipline problem more than anything else.
apply: If you've got a foreman who hasn't been through the full four weeks yet, watch how they run shift handover and write up an NCR — those two things are exactly what this program is built to fix.
